Police were also trying to stop people from reaching the capital in the first place. Independent journalist Raj Shekhar told Newslaundry that bus services into Delhi had been effectively halted. Travelling from Delhi towards Palwal and the KMP highway from 7 am, he counted three buses heading to Delhi between 7:30 and 9:30 am. A Haryana Roadways employee at Ballabhgarh told him buses were being diverted at KMP towards Kundli. Cab drivers said buses were being stopped at barricades beyond Palwal, and bus station staff had been told not to sell Delhi tickets. Shekhar said buses are being turned away 50 to 80 km outside the city. “People travel to Delhi for more than just the protest,” the roadways employee said. “How can the government just shut down buses like this? How can they stop people from moving around in their own country?” It is unclear whether the tactic will work. The 26-year-old cab driver who took Shekhar from Ballabhgarh to KMP and back said people would get off at Kundli and elsewhere and make their way in. “If not today, they will come tomorrow,” he said. Restrictions on media In Central Delhi, Newslaundry reporter Anmol Pritam was at Connaught Place by 6:42 am, watching Delhi Police detain people walking toward Jantar Mantar. Reporters were not allowed to cross the road to the area where people were being held. Police cited an SOP for media personnel, saying a designated space had been allotted to the press. Pritam said journalists were told that anyone stepping beyond it would be pushed back and threatened with detention. A team from Khabar Lahariya that tried to reach a bus carrying detainees was turned back. He noted that during an earlier protest, reporters could go up to Tolstoy Road or the Janpath Metro station. items.summary: Monu Yadav, alias Monu Manesar, the self-styled cow vigilante and Bajrang Dal leader, appeared in an Instagram video on October 9 warning protesters against attacking police personnel at the CJP protest scheduled for October 10. In the 2:15-minute clip, Monu Manesar said he was angry over violent protesters. “Our police personnel are being beaten up, our lady police officers are being treated inappropriately,” he said. “Me and my entire team are against it.” He then threatened anyone found to have attacked police. “If we find someone from the videos we saw, if they end up in front of us, they better save themselves because we can’t be held responsible for what we will do, Jai Shree Ram,” he said. Towards the end of the clip, he added: “Our teams are ready. Our teams are active and we will deactivate you, so take care.” The video was posted on the verified Instagram profile “mohitthehindu052”, which has 1,54,000 followers. It had garnered over 1,33,000 views within 24 hours. Speaking to Newslaundry from Gurugram, Monu Manesar said his team would be present at Jantar Mantar on October 10 and “we will not tolerate any wrongdoing against our country, our culture and our police personnel.” Asked about police violence against protesters, he said he had heard of it but had not seen video evidence of police touching protesters. “They may be cockroaches but we are HIT,” he said referring to the commonly used insecticide brand. Monu Manesar has been part of the Bajrang Dal for nearly a decade. Before his arrest, he regularly posted videos on social media documenting cow-vigilante activity, including raids and confrontations with people suspected of transporting cattle for slaughter. His activities came against the backdrop of tighter cow protection laws in Haryana. In 2019, the state added stricter provisions to the anti-cow slaughter law that the BJP government had passed in 2015. items.title: A walk to forget? Why Delhi High Court slapped ₹10,000 costs on advocate
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Friday imposed costs of ₹10,000 on an advocate for appearing in court virtually while walking in the garden. Justice Om Prakash Shukla said that the lawyer's conduct was in violation of the Electronic Evidence and Video Conferencing Rules, 2025. "Learned Counsel is appearing in this matter while walking in the garden and the connection is also not proper. This is in violation of the Electronic Evidence and Video Conferencing Rules, 2025 of this Court. Accordingly, costs of Rs.10,000/- is imposed on the learned counsel for the petitioner, to be deposited before the Delhi High Court Legal Services Committee within a week from today," the Court ordered. It added that on the next date of hearing on November 4, the counsel must appear in person. The Court passed the order while dealing with an arbitration petition. Notably, this is not the first time Justice Shukla has objected to persons appearing virtually in improper manner. Last month, he had fined a lawyer ₹1 lakh for appearing in court while sitting in a moving car. He observed that the convenience of virtual proceedings cannot come at the cost of courtroom decorum or disrupt the conduct of judicial proceedings.

items.title: Madhya Pradesh High Court seeks production of two Delhi-bound protestors detained ahead of CJP protest
items.summary: The Madhya Pradesh High Court on Friday directed the State police to produce before it two persons reportedly detained in connection with the upcoming Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest in Delhi on October 10. A bench of Chief Justice Alpesh Y Kogje and Justice Vivek Jain , however, also clarified that the police can make arrangements to ensure the safe return of the detainees to their family members. “It is also open for the State to produce the corpus before the Court prior to the returnable date with the prior notice to the other side,” the Court added. It passed the orders on Habeas Corpus petitions moved by Shardul Jitendra Buwa and Vishakha Prashant Londhe. Both of them hail from Maharashtra. The matter will be heard next on October 13. According to media reports, the police detained at least 30 Delhi-bound protesters at Bhopal, Itarsi and Gwalior railway stations. The protestors were travelling from Goa, Karnataka and Maharashtra. The October 10 protest in the national capital has been called by various opposition parties and youth organisations including the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP).

items.title: CJP protests: Contempt plea in Supreme Court alleges Delhi Metro stations closed despite court order
items.summary: A contempt of court petition has been filed before the Supreme Court alleging that Delhi Metro stations remained closed today despite the Court's October 9 order against a complete shutdown of public transport ahead of the proposed protests at Jantar Mantar by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP). The petition, filed by advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi, seeks initiation of contempt of court proceedings against Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar and Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) Chairperson D Thara for alleged wilful disobedience of the Court's directions. Tripathi has alleged that despite the order, DMRC announced that entry and exit gates at 45 Metro stations would remain closed from 9 PM on October 9 until 6 PM on October 10. According to the petitioner, he personally visited GTB Nagar and Vishwavidyalaya Metro stations around 9.30 PM on October 9 and found entry gates closed. At GTB Nagar, gates 1 and 2 were closed while gate 3 permitted only regulated exits. Tripathi claims to have video-recorded gate 2. At Vishwavidyalaya station, the entry gate was allegedly shut while only the exit gate remained open. Tripathi claims that when he visited Jantar Mantar around 8.30 PM, only police and paramilitary personnel were present. The petition has also alleged continued train cancellations and inadequate publicity of revised transport arrangements. The plea seeks directions to the officials concerned to appear personally before the Court and explain why contempt action should not be initiated. It also seeks immediate withdrawal of blanket restrictions and restoration of regulated transport services. On Friday, a Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana had said that there should not be complete closure of metro trains or other forms of transport. The intervened after petitions challenged restrictions on Metro and railway services ahead of protests called by the Cockroach Janta Party and other groups. The Court described the restrictions as "overreaching" and distinguished between regulating public transport and prohibiting it altogether. It recorded Solicitor General Tushar Mehta's assurance that authorities would reconsider the restrictions. The Court also required DMRC, railway authorities and Delhi Police (Traffic) to file compliance reports within four days. items.title: NCLT suspends functioning of Mumbai Bench's court VI due to vacancies
items.summary: The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) has ordered temporary suspension of functioning of court VI of its Mumbai Bench from October 13, citing vacancies in the posts of tribunal members. In an administrative order dated October 9, the NCLT directed that all cases pending before court VI be transferred to the five other courts of the Mumbai Bench. The suspension will remain in effect until further orders. " In view of the vacancies to the post of Members at the National Company Law Tribunal, Mumbai Bench, the functioning of Court no. VI Mumbai Bench is temporarily suspended, w.e.f. 13.10.2026, until further order ," the order stated. The decision was taken with the approval of the NCLT President under Rule 16(d) of the National Company Law Tribunal Rules, 2016. According to the order, pending matters have been divided among Courts I, II, III, IV and V of the Mumbai Bench. The redistribution covers cases filed under Sections 7, 9, 10 and 95 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), 2016. Cases filed under Section 7 of the IBC, which concerns insolvency proceedings initiated by financial creditors, have been divided into five groups based on their serial numbers in the annexure to the order. Similarly, matters initiated by operational creditors under Section 9 have been distributed among the remaining five courts. The tribunal has directed all concerned court officers to transfer and receive the relevant case records and list the matters on their next scheduled hearing dates in accordance with the last orders passed in those cases. The administrative decision comes amid vacancies affecting the functioning of the tribunal's Mumbai Bench. However, the order does not specify the number of vacant posts or indicate when court VI is likely to resume functioning. [Read Notification]

items.title: Delhi High Court asks Amitabh Bachchan to appear personally if he wants to continue personality rights case
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Friday said veteran actor Amitabh Bachchan will have to appear personally before the Court if he wishes to pursue his personality rights suit [Amitabh Bachchan v Rajat Nagi & Ors] . Justice Purushaindra Kumar Kaurav said that if the Bachchan is unable to settle the matter between one or more defendants, and he then wants to pursue the case in court, he will have to be present in Court. The Court passed the direction on October 9 while granting Bachchan time to complete the formalities of an amicable settlement reached with some of the defendants. The Court was informed that although a settlement had been arrived at with some of the defendants, it could not be formally signed due to logistical issues on the actor’s part. “In the event of non-settlement or incomplete settlement, if the plaintiff wishes to pursue the suit on any of the claims or issues, the plaintiff shall remain personally present on the next date of hearing, enabling the Court to exercise its powers under Order X Rule 2 read with Order V Rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and Section 168 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023,” the Court ordered. Justice Purushaindra Kumar Kaurav Bachchan had filed the suit seeking a permanent injunction to protect his personality rights. The High Court had granted an ex parte ad interim injunction in his favour on November 25, 2022. During the proceedings, the parties explored the possibility of resolving the dispute amicably through mediation. On October 9, the Court was told that a settlement has been reached with some of the defendants, but a formal agreement is yet to be executed. Bachchan was represented by advocates Dhruv Anand, Dhananjay Khanna and Bhavya Verma. [Read Order]

items.title: Bengaluru police rejig: 21 new stations proposed under five new commissionerates
items.summary: Bengaluru’s police network is set for a major overhaul, with five commissionerates proposed to oversee an expanded jurisdiction and 21 new police stations planned. However, the Finance Department has approved only 11 of the proposed stations so far. According to The New Indian Express , the proposed commissionerates—Central, North, South, West and East—will be headed by officers of Inspector General of Police (IGP) or Deputy Inspector General of Police (DIGP) rank. They will function under the Chief Commissioner of Police. Currently, Bengaluru City Police has 11 law and order divisions and four traffic divisions, each headed by a Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP). Under the proposed restructuring, the five commissionerates will have a total of 14 law and order divisions and five traffic divisions. Six police stations from Bengaluru Rural district—Sarjapura, Jigani, Attibele, Anekal, Bannerghatta and Suryanagar—will be brought under the DCP (Electronics City) division of the Bengaluru South Commissionerate. Kaggalipura police station, currently under Bengaluru South district police, will be placed under the DCP (South) division. The East Commissionerate is proposed to have new police stations at Kasturinagar (RM Nagar), Kodathi and Bidarahalli, along with two other stations whose names are yet to be finalised. In the West Commissionerate, Andrahalli and Kadabagere will be added as new police stations under the DCP (Peenya) division. The seven proposed new traffic police stations are Kothanur, Marathahalli, Avalahalli, Hebbagodi, Attibele, RR Nagar and Madanayakanahalli. The restructuring aims to expand the police administration’s coverage through additional divisions and police stations across Bengaluru.

items.title: Kerala HC orders fresh probe into Balabhaskar’s death, says CBI failed to examine doubts
items.summary: The Kerala High Court has ordered a fresh investigation by a senior Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) officer into the 2018 death of renowned violinist Balabhaskar, criticising the agency for conducting a “casual and lackadaisical” probe into 20 suspicious circumstances flagged by the court in an earlier order. Justice G Girish, in an order dated October 9, set aside the Thiruvananthapuram Chief Judicial Magistrate Court’s December 23, 2025, decision to reject a plea for further investigation filed by Balabhaskar’s parents, K C Unni and B Santhakumari. The court directed the CBI to entrust the investigation to an officer of “proven integrity” not below the rank of Additional Superintendent of Police. It also directed the agency to issue the necessary orders within two weeks of receiving a copy of the judgment. “The course of procedure adopted by the Inspector of Police towards arriving at the aforesaid findings cannot be said to be one which behove the status of skill, tactics and expertise which are expected from a premier investigating agency like the CBI,” the court observed. Balabhaskar died on October 2, 2018, from injuries sustained in a car accident on September 25 that year, near the CRPF camp at Pallippuram on the National Highway in Thiruvananthapuram. His one-and-a-half-year-old daughter, Thejaswini Bala, died shortly after the accident. His wife, Lakshmi, survived, while the car was being driven by Arjun K Narayanan. The case was initially investigated by the state police, followed by the Crime Branch, before being handed over to the CBI after suspicions were raised about a possible connection between the accident and a gold-smuggling network. The CBI concluded that the incident was an accident and filed its final report in 2021. However, in an order dated October 5, 2023, the High Court directed further investigation into whether there was a conspiracy or a connection between gold-smuggling activities and the accident. The court identified 20 suspicious circumstances that required further examination. These included the circumstances surrounding the family's sudden return from Thrissur on the night before the accident; the collection and subsequent possession of Balabhaskar's mobile phones; the role of Prakash Thampi, a close friend who was later arrested in a gold-smuggling case; and questions concerning the handling of evidence. items.title: CJI Surya Kant to attend NLSIU convocation in Bengaluru, no livestreaming of event
items.summary: Nearly two months after Bengaluru’s National Law School of India University (NLSIU) cancelled the convocation for its students for objecting to Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant attending the event, the university has announced its decision to hold the convocation on October 17. However unlike in the past, the convocation would neither be live streamed nor would phones be allowed inside. The convocation at NLSIU was cancelled after its students had issued a statement expressing solidarity with NALSAR Hyderabad graduates. Students at NALSAR had protested CJI Suryakant being invited for their convocation. NALSAR students had argued that they did not want to accept their certificates from the CJI as he had referred to the youth of India as ‘cockroaches’. They also criticised him for his unwillingness to listen to a plea in the Supreme Court over the police violence against protestors demanding then Union Education minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar. However, following the dissent, Bar Council of India (BCI) Chairman Manan Kumar Mishra threatened to prohibit the enrolment of NALSAR students in the bar. While Chairman Manan Kumar rescinded his statements a day later, NLSIU students said they expressed their “strong disapproval of the CJI (and Mishra) attending the convocation of NLSIU for the same reasons.” It remains unclear if BCI Chairman Manan Kumar will be attending the convocation. The NLSIU registrar issued a statement on August 27, announcing that the convocation scheduled for September 12 was being cancelled due to “unavoidable circumstances”. This announcement came after talks with students failed to reach a consensus. In the last few weeks, several rounds of discussions have happened between the college administration, students and alumni. It was eventually decided that the CJI would attend the event. items.title: ‘No intent to outrage modesty’: Kerala HC acquits man convicted for elbowing woman’s chest
items.summary: The Kerala High Court has acquitted a man who was convicted of outraging a woman's modesty after allegedly striking her on the chest with his elbow, holding that the act attributed to him did not establish criminal intention. The Court therefore ruled that he cannot be convicted under Section 354 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), which deals with using criminal force to outrage the modesty of a woman. Justice Jobin Sebastian, in an order dated September 30, 2026, allowed a criminal revision petition filed by Rajendran, the accused in the case, setting aside his conviction and sentence by the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-I, Chalakudy, subsequently upheld by the Additional Sessions Court-III, Thrissur. “I have no hesitation in holding that the necessary mens rea to constitute an offence under Section 354 of the IPC is lacking in this case,” the court observed. Mens rea is the legal term for the intention to commit a crime. The case originated from an incident alleged to have occurred at around 10 am on March 26, 2002, when the complainant was walking along the Urumbankunnu Panchayat Road. According to the prosecution, Rajendran struck her on the right side of her chest with his elbow, thereby outraging her modesty. The trial court found him guilty under Section 354 of the IPC on August 23, 2004, and sentenced him to one month of simple imprisonment and a fine of Rs 1,000. He was also sentenced to another month of simple imprisonment in default of paying the fine. The appellate court dismissed his appeal on October 30, 2006, upholding both the conviction and sentence. In his revision petition before the High Court, Rajendran challenged the findings of the two courts, arguing that the evidence had not been properly assessed and that the possibility of false implication had not been considered. His counsel pointed out that a case had been registered against the complainant's husband based on a complaint filed by Rajendran before the alleged incident. The complainant had admitted during cross-examination that such a case existed; the court noted. The defence argued that this prior dispute raised the possibility of false implication. The defence further alleged contradictions in the testimonies of the two witnesses and a one-day delay in lodging the first information report. items.title: CJP protest: Internet shut down, metros cancelled despite SC asking to ensure services
items.summary: Ahead of the protest called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar, orders have been issued to suspend mobile internet services within a 4-km radius of the Janpath-Kartavya Path crossing in New Delhi from 10 pm on October 9 until 10 pm on October 10. The Ministry of Home Affairs approved the temporary suspension, ANI reported. The order covers all mobile internet services in the area. The CJP is demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, alleging that the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls has disenfranchised crores of voters along with other irregularities. A day earlier, the Supreme Court questioned the proposed closures of metro stations and train cancellations ahead of the protest, calling notifications imposing a complete ban on essential public transport “overreaching”. A bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, with Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, said the entire city could not be shut down in the name of managing a protest. The Court asked authorities to ensure that metro and rail services continued in a regulated manner and directed the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC), railway authorities and Delhi Police (Traffic) to submit compliance reports within four days. Before the Court’s intervention, Delhi Police had asked the DMRC to reduce train frequency and close entry and exit gates at 57 stations from 9 pm on October 9. The DMRC later announced that gates at 45 stations would remain closed until 6 pm on October 10, while interchange facilities would remain available at affected stations, except New Delhi. Indian Railways also cancelled trains scheduled to arrive at New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin stations between 4 am and 2 pm on October 10. A separate report said 38 Delhi-bound trains were cancelled. The Sarai Kale Khan and New Ashok Nagar Namo Bharat stations were also scheduled to remain closed until 10 pm. Meanwhile, on October 10, advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi filed a contempt plea alleging that authorities had not complied with the Supreme Court’s directions. He claimed that gates at 45 metro stations remained closed despite the Court’s order, and said he filmed locked entry gates at GTB Nagar and Vishwavidyalaya stations at around 9.30 pm on October 9. The plea also alleges that train cancellations continued, that revised travel arrangements were not adequately publicised and that police and paramilitary personnel were present at Jantar Mantar around 8.30 pm

items.title: Dhruv Rathee, CJP leaders detained ahead of Delhi protest against CEC
items.summary: YouTuber Dhruv Rathee, Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) legal head Ratna Singh, and several other protesters were reportedly detained on Saturday, October 10, ahead of the party’s proposed demonstration at Jantar Mantar in Delhi. The party has demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of electoral irregularities and concerns surrounding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Delhi police detained Dhruv Rathee from his residence in Sector 56, Gurugram, while Ratna Singh was reportedly detained from her residence in Delhi. Reports also said around 150 protesters had been detained by morning. Several content creators were among those detained in Dhaula Kuan, according to live updates. Mehr Pasricha, head of CJP policy division, was also reportedly detained ahead of the protest. The detentions came amid heightened security across Delhi, with police and paramilitary personnel deployed at key locations, border checkpoints, railway stations and other sensitive areas. The police have denied permission for the proposed demonstration, citing inadequate notice, non-compliance with prescribed guidelines and concerns over public safety and law and order. Around 25,000 police and paramilitary personnel were deployed across the city, while other reports put the expected deployment at more than 35,000 personnel. Security arrangements included barricades, drone surveillance, vehicle checks and personnel equipped with body cameras. Police also intensified checks at the Delhi borders with Uttar Pradesh and Haryana to prevent unauthorised groups from entering New Delhi. Security was tightened at the Chilla, Ghazipur, Badarpur, Aya Nagar and Sarhaul border areas, among other locations. Deputy Commissioner of Police Anant Mittal told IANS, “Our effort is to ensure that everything remains peaceful and law and order is maintained.” Traffic and airport restrictions The Delhi Traffic Police issued an advisory warning of possible traffic diversions at 30 locations from 6 am on Saturday, depending on the prevailing law-and-order situation. The affected stretches include areas around Jantar Mantar, Mandi House, Connaught Place, Patel Chowk, Rail Bhawan, Janpath, and Parliament Street. Additional Commissioner of Police (Traffic) DK Gupta said, “If any protests take place, we will formulate diversion plans accordingly. items.title: ‘Open Jantar Mantar, metro stations, stop detaining activists’: CPI MP writes to PM Modi
items.summary: Communist Party of India (CPI) Rajya Sabha MP P Sandosh Kumar has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, urging the Union government to reopen Jantar Mantar for protests, stop detaining activists and ensure that citizens can exercise their constitutional right to peaceful assembly. In a letter dated October 9, Sandosh Kumar alleged that repeated attempts by protesters to reach Jantar Mantar, a designated protest site in Delhi, had been met with barricades, detentions and police action. He said the protests stemmed from allegations of electoral malpractice, referred to by protesters as “vote-chori”, and called for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. “I am compelled to write this letter because every method of reaching out to your insensitive government has been met with barricades and lathis,” the CPI MP wrote. He further noted that Article 19 of the Constitution guarantees citizens the freedom to assemble peacefully and argued that elected representatives, students, youth and activists have the right to protest against what he described as the “complete collapse of India’s electoral democracy”. “Our demand is very simple: we want to peacefully protest against our collective grievances over the complete collapse of India’s electoral democracy and demand the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar,” he wrote. Sandosh Kumar alleged that the government had responded to protesters through detentions, arrests and house arrests instead of engaging with them. Claiming that more than 47,000 security personnel had been deployed in Central Delhi alone, he said even women MPs and activists had faced police action while attempting to reach the designated protest site. “This is a state of emergency,” he wrote. The MP also alleged that activists were being arrested and detained at locations more than 1,000 kilometres from Delhi, while trains heading to the national capital were being cancelled. He argued that the restrictions were causing inconvenience to ordinary citizens, including through traffic congestion and metro station closures. “I wish to make it categorically clear that turning Delhi into a military cantonment will not deter us. We will raise our voice. No amount of barricading, intimidation or repression can take away our fundamental right to protest,” he said.
